title: Optimized protocol for live imaging of overnutrition-elicited interactions between immune cells and β cells in zebrafish
protocol: Generate breeders for the following lines to adulthood.
Raise Tg(acta1:dnigf1ra-EGFP)vu530 (referred to as zMIR).
Raise Tg(ins:H2BmCherry)vu513.
Crossbreed zMIR with Tg(ins:H2BmCherry); Tg(mpeg1:EGFP).
Raise Tg(LyzC:DsRED2).
Raise Tg(LyzC:GFP).
Identify fish with the desired genotypes.
Set up appropriate breeders to generate progenies with the desired genotypes.
Use a transfer pipette to carefully move the desired larvae individually into a Petri dish.
Raise the larvae to adults in the fish facility.
Raise breeder lines that are tnfa+/−.
Perform PCR genotyping to determine the tnfa genotypes.
Feed larvae older than 6 dpf with Paramecium or 1% egg yolk medium twice daily.
Starve larvae only if necessary for experimental purposes, as starvation may lead to misleading outcomes.
Determine genotypes using fluorescent markers and/or PCR.
Raise fish to adulthood.
Generate fish of desired genotypes for the experiment.
Harvest embryos using a strainer, rinse gently with egg water.
Collect embryos in fresh egg water (0.2 g/L Instant Ocean Salt) in 10 cm Petri dishes.
Place Petri dishes into a 28°C incubator.
Check embryos daily to remove dead embryos and detached chorions.
Identify fish with desired cell lineage markers at 4 dpf.
Add 150 μL of Tricaine stock to a Petri dish containing larvae in 15 mL egg water.
Wait approximately 1 minute until all larvae are anesthetized.
Examine larvae under a stereo fluorescent microscope (Zeiss Discovery V12) to identify individuals with desired genotypes.
Transfer zMIR+ and zMIR- larvae one by one separately into a cell strainer sitting in a Petri dish with 15 mL egg water using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Transfer each cell strainer to another Petri dish containing egg water.
Gently agitate the Petri dish to eliminate Tricaine.
Transfer all fish in the strainer to a Petri dish with 25 mL of fresh egg water.
Perform the screening process rapidly and gently.
Avoid damaging the larvae or immersing them in tricaine solution for too long.
Put the dishes back into the 28°C incubator until the next step.
Feed larvae with Paramecium (400 paramecia per larva) if older than 6 dpf.
Alternatively, feed with 1% egg yolk medium (25 mL for 30 min for up to 80 larvae).
Perform the 3-day overnutrition experiment.
Harvest egg yolk.
Add an equal amount of 0.3x Danieau’s solution to the egg yolk-containing conical tube.
Generate a 50% stock by vigorous vortexing.
Prepare working medium by mixing 5 mL of the 50% stock with 45 mL of 0.3x Danieau’s solution.
Add 25 mL of the 5% egg yolk medium and less than 20 larvae to a clean 50 mL beaker.
Transfer the larvae into a sterile cell strainer placed in a Petri dish.
Transfer larvae into a 50 mL clean beaker with 25 mL of the 5% egg yolk medium.
Put the beaker into a 28°C incubator.
Stir the medium every 2 hours as sediments accumulate.
Transfer larvae clear of egg yolk into a Petri dish with 0.3x Danieau’s solution.
Take 5 mL of the 50% egg yolk emulsion after standing for 5 minutes.
Add it into a 50 mL centrifuge tube containing 45 mL of 0.3x Danieau solution.
Close the lid and shake on a tube vortexer at maximum speed for 2 minutes.
Pour 25 mL of the resulting 5% egg yolk medium into a 50 mL glass beaker.
If treating larvae with an inhibitor, dilute the compound in the appropriate solvent as a stock (≥1000x) and then to the desired working concentration in the 5% egg yolk medium.
Add the same volume of the solvent used for the inhibitor into the 5% egg yolk medium for the control group.
Set up the overnutrition experiment for larvae.
Collect larvae for the experiment.
Place a sterile cell strainer in a petri dish containing 25 mL of 0.3x Danieau’s solution.
Transfer all larvae from the original dish to the sterile cell strainer using a transfer pipette.
Remove excess liquid by taking the cell strainer out of the Danieau’s solution and tapping it on a clean paper towel quickly.
Remove excess Danieau’s solution from the cell strainer.
Gently transfer larvae into the cell strainer without damaging them.
Submerge the cell strainer in a beaker containing 5% yolk medium to release larvae.
Transfer an equal number of larvae to each experimental group beaker.
Do not exceed 20 larvae per 25 mL or 40 larvae per 50 mL of egg yolk medium to avoid hypoxia and stress.
Stir the sediments in the beaker with a transfer pipette every 2 hours.
Place the bore of the transfer pipette to the bottom of the beaker and gently pipette up and down to break up the sediments.
Use a new transfer pipette for each beaker, especially when using drugs or compounds.
Transfer larvae to nutrient-free medium after 8 hours in the egg yolk medium.
Rinse residual egg yolk medium off larvae by gently stirring cell strainer in Petri dish with 25 mL 0.3x Danieau’s solution.
Move larvae to new Petri dish containing 25 mL fresh 0.3x Danieau’s solution using transfer pipette.
Remove all residual egg yolk sediments and replenish Petri dish with fresh 0.3x Danieau’s solution.
If inhibitor is needed, dilute stock into 0.3x Danieau’s solution to desired working concentration.
Add same volume of solvent (e.g., DMSO) into 0.3x Danieau’s solution for control group.
Place Petri dish containing larvae back into 28°C incubator for 16 h.
Repeat steps for rinsing, moving, and adding solutions twice more for complete 3-day overnutrition experiment.
Use fresh 5% egg yolk each day to avoid high microbial load that impacts fish health.
Transfer the larvae into a 35 mm Glass Bottom Dish.
Anesthetize the larvae with Tricane stock to achieve a final concentration of 0.16 g/L.
Remove most of the medium with a transfer pipette.
Remove residual medium using a transfer pipette with a 10 μL pipette tip attached.
Add 750 μL of pre-heated 1.2% LMA at the center of the glass bottom dish using a P1000 pipette.
Position the larvae on their right side using two insulin syringe needles.
Allow the LMA to solidify.
Add 750 μL of 0.3x Danieau’s solution containing Tricaine at the periphery of the dish after the LMA has solidified.
Submerge the gel with the 0.3x Danieau’s solution.
Check the larvae under a stereo microscope to ensure proper positioning and immersion in the solution.
Do not transfer more than 4 larvae into a dish.
Aspirate most of the medium in the bottom glass dish using a transfer pipette.
Attach a 10 μL pipette tip to the transfer pipette and aspirate residual medium carefully.
Take an aliquot of LMA from a 42°C block heater and add 750 μL of LMA to cover the larvae.
Position the larvae so that their right-hand side is close to the glass bottom using needles of two insulin syringes.
Position the larvae carefully for immobilization.
Add 750 μl of 0.3x Danieau’s solution containing tricaine gently around the dish periphery once the LMA gel solidifies.
Submerge the LMA gel with the medium without disturbing it.
Cover the dish with a lid and return to the incubator for imaging preparation.
Start the LSM 780 Laser Scanning Microscope according to manufacturer's instructions.
Use a 20x objective (NA 0.5) for live imaging.
Heat up the environment chamber to 30°C.
Perform live imaging on the principal islet.
Transfer the glass bottom dish to the chamber.
Incubate the larvae at 30°C for at least 20 minutes before imaging.
Confirm that the larvae are laying on the righthand side before beginning the imaging session.
Set up the z-stack settings.
Take 512 × 512 volumetric time-lapse images at 15-second or 30-second intervals with a z-step size of 1.2 μm and an average total thickness of 35 μm.
Maintain the power of all excitation lasers as low as possible (<1.5%) to minimize phototoxicity.
Genotype the larvae after live imaging if necessary.
Aspirate the medium using a transfer pipette carefully.
Pick up individual larvae from the LMA using tweezers.
Place each larva into an 8-strip tube of PCR tubes.
Add 100 μL 50 mM NaOH to each tube.
Incubate in a PCR machine at 95°C for 30 min.
Add 20 μL 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) to neutralize the lysate.
Perform PCR using Genotyping Primers.
Run the reaction using specified PCR cycling conditions in a thermocycler.
Run the PCR product on a 3% agarose gel to distinguish mutant, heterozygous, and wild-type larvae.
Convert the LSM file of images into an Imaris Image File using Imaris File Converter.
Open the images with Imaris.
Track the movement of macrophages or neutrophils according to the reference manual.
Click on the spot icon in Imaris.
Unselect “Start Creation with slice view” option.
Click on the “Start” button.
Select GFP in the “channel” pulldown menu.
Click on "slice view" button, zoom in to measure the largest distance between 2 points within a GFP labelled cell.
Key in the XY diameter measured as d in the 3D view.
Each cell visible in the channel is now automatically labelled with a spot.
Click on the next button until you see the “Algorithm” pulldown menu.
Choose “Autoregressive Motion”.
Measure the MaxDistance between adjacent frames of a spot.
In “Slice View”, select a spot and measure the distance it has shifted in the next frame in 4 consecutive frames.
Round up the largest distance as Max Distance.
Key in the MaxGapSize. We always use 3.
Click the play button to track all selected images in the video.
Export the tracking images.

Quantify the number of macrophages that were in or near (within a defined diameter) the islet or the number of times a neutrophil was detected in the islet within the imaged period in both control and experiment groups.
Manually confirm the number frame by frame.
Enter the data points into the GraphPad Prism 8.0.
Analyze the data through one-way ANOVA.
